newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden inflation below zero, 1st time in 37 years.
newsitem.headline: Sweden inflation below zero, 1st time in 37 years.

text.p: Swedish year-on-year inflation fell below zero in October for the first time since 1959, Statistics Sweden said on Thursday.
"From October 1995 until October 1996, consumer prices fell on average by 0.1 percent," Statistics Sweden said in a statement. That compares with a 2.7-percent inflation rate a year ago.
The October inflation figure was even below the government's aim to keep inflation between one and two percent over the next two years.
The negative figure was recorded after consumer prices remained unchanged between September and October this year.
Statistics Sweden said lower interest rate costs and lower value added tax on food were the main reasons behind the fall in prices.
"Food prices have fallen by 6.7 percent (over the year), which has reduced the overall price level by 1.0 percent," Statistics Sweden said.

"Lower interest rate costs have contributed a further 1.1 percent to the fall. Other living costs have however risen, including rent, property tax and taxes on fuel. Living costs in total have therefore, lifted the price level by 0.4 percent."
